In [[mathematics]], an '''ordinary singularity''' of an [[algebraic curve]] is a [[Singular point of a curve|singular point]] of [[multiplicity (mathematics)|multiplicity]] ''r'' where the ''r'' tangents at the point are distinct {{harv|Walker|1950|loc=p. 54}}.
In higher dimensions the literature on [[algebraic geometry]] contains many inequivalent definitions of ordinary singular points.
